- uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Pinned release must carry signed provenance
        run: bash scripts/check_install_pin.sh

  quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, model-switch-reg, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-goldens, flutter-app-lock-smoke, office-addin-suite, extension-size-gate]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "installer-reg  = ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "goldens     = ${{ needs.flutter-app-goldens.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
          echo "office-addin  = ${{ needs.office-addin-suite.result }}"
          echo "ext-size-gate = ${{ needs.extension-size-gate.result }}"
          echo "model-switch-reg = ${{ needs.model-switch-reg.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_REG: ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_GOLDENS: ${{ needs.flutter-app-goldens.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
          R_OFFICE_ADDIN: ${{ needs.office-addin-suite.result }}
          R_EXT_SIZE: ${{ needs.extension-size-gate.result }}
          R_MODEL_SWITCH_REG: ${{ needs.model-switch-reg.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-portability:$R_INSTALLER_REG" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "model-switch-reg:$R_MODEL_SWITCH_REG" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-goldens:$R_GOLDENS" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE" "office-addin-suite:$R_OFFICE_ADDIN" "extension-size-gate:$R_EXT_SIZE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke|flutter-app-goldens|installer-portability|office-addin-suite|extension-size-gate)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ -n "$dart_blocker" ]; then dart_ok=false; else dart_ok=true; fi
          echo "dart_ok=$dart_ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Aggregate verdicts AFTER the export — branch protection is
          # unchanged: ANY red leg (package or platform) still fails this
          # required check; only the PUBLISH gate ignores platform reds.
          [ -z "$dart_blocker" ] || fail "$dart_blocker"
          [ "$platform_red" = "false" ] || fail "a platform/native leg is red — the aggregate is red; dart_ok stays true (publish is not gated on platform legs, #1368), see the leg results above"
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.

# gh-1655: pre-install the Flutter-pinned NDK so Gradle configuration
      # never auto-installs it mid-build — that path has no retry, and one
      # truncated download ("Error on ZipFile unknown archive") red'd this
      # leg and the aggregate Quality gate. Same hardening as the seed.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall

      # gh-2072: prewarm the sqlite3 hook cache for the APK ABI triples
      # (armeabi-v7a/arm64-v8a/x86_64) before the debug APK build — the
      # build-time hook downloads the prebuilt libsqlite3 per triple with a
      # single unretried attempt (gh-2072: one 504 error page red'd this leg
      # at v1.0.697). package-roots is REQUIRED here (gh-2072 review thread
      # 3): this job resolves ONLY flutter_app (via flutter-pub-get), so the
      # `.` default would read a root package config that never exists —
      # the PR's own run red'd this leg exactly that way.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
        with:
          targets: android
          package-roots: flutter_app

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS (debug, unsigned)
    # The owner's box carries Xcode 27 — the Duo layout channel's iOS 27
    # fold APIs (UIView.reservedRegions, UITraitCollection.verticalBarEdge)
    # do not exist in any hosted SDK (Xcode 26.6 tops out at iOS 26.5).
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    # gh-2314: raised 30 → 150 so the WasmRun restore step's worst case
    # (a full slow-window download, see the restore step below) plus the
    # healthy pub-get/pods/build tail still fits inside the job — the
    # gh-2070 doctrine: a ceiling sized to the healthy wall turns one
    # contention window into a release-kill (build-ios red'd twice on
    # v1.0.748 under the old 30-min ceiling). Pinned by
    # test/ci_build_ios_wasmrun_budget_guard_test.dart (AC5).
    timeout-minutes: 150
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # gh-1736 guard (test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart): a
      # self-hosted leg may pair subosito/flutter-action with cache —
      # never cache: true (the action's shared-cache poisoning is a
      # hosted-only convenience). The box keeps its own warm pub cache.
      # Exact patch (#1100 parity + #1431): the golden baselines and the
      # nightly leg pin 3.47.4 — a release-path build must share it.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.50.0'
          channel: stable

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

- name: Probe every landing-page release link
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --landing site/index.html
      - name: Probe the full required asset set
        env:
          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --smoke "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

  # Advance the vpinned release marker to the freshly signed tag. PURE
  # RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION — no commits, no pushes: pin_release.sh
  # re-verifies the target's signature itself (fail-closed), then uploads
  # the PINNED_VERSION asset to the standing `vpinned` release. Runs after
  # release-provenance so the signed SHA256SUMS it checks are already
  # published. The marker is only a pointer — installers verify the pointed
  # release's signature against the committed trust anchor, so a tampered
  # marker degrades to a DoS, never a bad binary.
  install-pin-bump:
    name: Advance vpinned marker
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # always(): when release-provenance FAILS (e.g. the binaries/signature
    # upload race), plain needs-gating leaves this job SKIPPED — and a
    # `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so the marker stays
    # stale forever (v1.0.483: publish+provenance flaked, the recovery rerun
    # went green, the marker never advanced). With always() the job RUNS
    # even after a failed provenance: pin_release.sh's own pre-move
    # provenance gate (check_install_pin.sh with FA_PIN_TARGET) fails the
    # job loudly instead of moving the marker — and a FAILED job IS part of
    # rerun --failed, so the recovery cascade reaches it.
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Point the vpinned marker at ${{ github.ref_name }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/pin_release.sh "${{ github.ref_name }}"

  installer-smoke:
    name: Installer smoke
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: [binaries, release-provenance]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Depends on binaries — no !cancelled() needed here: the skip chain is
    # already broken upstream by the binaries job's own guard (fa#456).
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            kind: ps1
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            kind: sh
          - os: macos-latest
            kind: sh
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (PowerShell)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./site/install.ps1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (sh)
        if: matrix.kind == 'sh'
        shell: bash
        env:
          FA_INSTALL_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin
        run: sh ./site/install.sh

      - name: Smoke the installed binary (Windows)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
        run: '& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Fa\bin\fa.exe" --version'

      - name: Smoke the installed binary (Unix)
        if: matrix.kind == 'sh'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -x "${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin/fa" ]; then
            fa_path="${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin/fa"
          else
            fa_path="$HOME/.local/bin/fa"
          fi
          # macOS downloads are quarantined by Gatekeeper; the installer strips
          # the attribute, but harden the smoke test in case it ever regresses.
          if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then
            xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$fa_path" 2>/dev/null || true
          fi

# tree: release-pending never blocks dispatch arms (gh-1551) and
  # release-dedupe is false for non-release events (gh-1625 AC3).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref. Tag pushes: the
    # release gate (gh-2290).
    if: always() && ((github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) || (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')))
    permissions:
      actions: write # gh workflow run — the tag-arm retrigger (gh-2290)
      contents: write
    steps:
      # gh-2290: the trip decision runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's
      # empty workspace has no scripts/ (the exit-127 class reddened the
      # dedupe pre-check on every arm, runs 38696670029/38696668627). The
      # checkout must be UNCONDITIONAL — the trip step runs on every arm
      # this job reaches, and a skipped checkout would empty the trip
      # output. Shallow: the script never reads history.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      # One jobs call in a SINGLE valid document (steps arrays are
      # embedded per job — no per-job follow-ups; `gh api --paginate`
      # concatenates page bodies and jq then reads only the first page —

      # fixture-self-tested trip decision (scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh;
      # static-gate selftest: scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh). It trips
      # ONLY on the timeout-kill signature — job conclusion `failure` OR
      # `cancelled` (the v1.0.745 kill landed as plain `cancelled`) with
      # at least one `cancelled` step and NO `failed` step — and never on
      # a real test failure (a step failed, regardless of which step is
      # last), a skip, or a cancelled never-started job.

        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          gh run view "$RUN_ID" --repo "$REPO" --json jobs > watchdog-jobs.json

        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"

      # ── Tag arm (gh-2290): dispatch a fresh gate run on the tag ref ────
      # ONE retrigger max per tag (issue #194 loop-guard rule): a prior
      # workflow_dispatch run for this tag ref means the retrigger already
      # fired for this kill — never chain dispatches on a stuck pool.
      - name: Retrigger the tag gate (dispatch, fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          prior=$(gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch "$REF" \
            --event workflow_dispatch \
            --json databaseId --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
          if [ "${prior:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::a workflow_dispatch gate run already exists for $REF — not re-firing (one retrigger max per tag, gh-2290)"
            exit 0
          fi
          gh workflow run ci.yml --ref "$REF"
          echo "::notice::dispatched a fresh ci.yml gate run on $REF (watchdog degraded-runner retrigger, gh-2290)"

# jobs (gh-1172); the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no
    # branch push), but remains the release-path actor (gh-1402).
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      (github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true)) &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (schedule, releaseDispatch — gh-1537 retired the main-push
      # trigger, so there is no push arm) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push, nothing else. gh-1801: auto_release.sh no longer
          # creates the GitHub Release (an asset-less create publishes an
          # empty `latest`) — the tag-run binaries job owns creation.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh-1801 (rework): no GH_TOKEN is exported here anymore —
          # auto_release.sh no longer calls `gh` at all (the asset-less
          # create published an empty `latest` and broke `fa update`; the
          # binaries job owns creation, draft-first). The tag push rides
          # the checkout App token above (gh-1172).
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64

binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own GREEN push run IS
    # the gate (the dedupe lookup fires only on conclusion == "success") —
    # the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
...
  release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      # gh-1832: PUBLISH-BLOCKING required-assets gate. The single source of
      # truth is scripts/release_required_assets.txt, consumed by
      # scripts/assert_release_assets.sh. v1.0.635 published without
      # fa-extension.zip because the extension's only producer (the daily
      # build-macos.yml build-extension leg) attached it to a "latest+1"
      # draft while this train published the tagged release — every leg
      # green, nothing asserted the published set. A missing asset here
      # fails the release run loudly and leaves the release a DRAFT (the
      # previous release stays latest) instead of publishing a partial one.
      - name: Assert required release assets (gh-1832 gate)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # gh-1801 (rework): THE publish point of the train. The release
          # now carries every fa-* asset AND the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) —
          # the first moment `fa update` can actually serve it (it
          # hard-fails without the signed checksums, bin/self_manage.dart).
          # Flip draft=false + latest here and ONLY here: a red provenance
          # leaves the previous release as latest (safe degradation)
          # instead of stranding a provenance-less one (the v1.0.630
          # empty/partial-latest window class).
          #
          # gh-2042 (BLOCKING review thread): the flip must never drag the
          # `latest` badge backwards. The drift remediation
          # (scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh) re-requests THIS job for
          # an old drifted tag; a job rerun re-executes this step with the
          # original run's ref, and an unconditional --latest would
          # re-flag that older release as Latest — pointing every
          # `fa update` client DOWN at it (the re-signed manifest would
          # make the downgrade pass provenance). Carry --latest ONLY when
          # the release is still a draft (the normal publish point,
          # gh-1801) or already the current latest; otherwise publish the
          # re-signed state without touching the badge.
          is_draft=$(gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)
          current_latest=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ "$is_draft" = "true" ] || [ "$current_latest" = "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" ]; then
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          else
            # Re-sign remediation of a non-latest tag: publish state is
            # already correct — never drag the latest badge backwards
            # (gh-2042).
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          fi

      # gh-1899: the flip above publishes exactly ONE release object, but
      # GitHub does not atomically enforce one release per tag — two train
      # legs racing the lazy draft create can BOTH succeed (v1.0.641, run
      # 40163369302: twin drafts 87 ms apart), and the unpicked twin then
      # rots until the 24h sweeper deletes it and files a recurring sweep
      # issue. The tag is published and servable now: reclaim this run's
      # twin drafts. Success-path only — a red provenance keeps the draft
      # as the rerun --failed recovery vessel.
      # Best-effort by design (gh-1899 review): the flip above already
      # published the release — a cleanup-only API blip here must NOT fail
      # the provenance job (release-asset-smoke gates on its result and
      # would silently skip for a release that is actually fine). Warn
      # and stay green; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop.
      - name: Reclaim orphaned draft twins (gh-1899)
        if: success()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_dedupe.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"

  # Train-level draft lifecycle guard (issue #282, gh-2230): this train is
  # the PUBLISH OWNER of every staged draft (gh-1801 rework —
  # release-provenance above is the sole --draft=false --latest flip), but
  # the per-creating-job guards cover only their own job's failure. A train
  # that dies upstream of the publish point (core tests → quality-gate red
  # → binaries skipped → release-provenance SKIPPED) used to orphan the
  # staged draft: the creating run's jobs all succeeded (their guards never
  # fire), the failed train is superseded and never rerun, and
  # verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only — so the draft rotted
  # exactly 24h until the daily sweeper deleted it and filed the recurring
  # sweep issue (gh-2230, v1.0.728). This job runs AFTER the publish point
  # settled — needs release-provenance + always(), so it fires on failed AND
  # cancelled trains and never on the success path's result (the script
  # no-ops on a published release). The script deletes ONLY when the
  # publish point is unreachable (result == 'skipped' — rerun --failed
  # never resurrects skipped jobs): drafts for THIS train's tag whose
  # owner-marker run has completed (scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh).
  # A failed/cancelled provenance is rerunnable, so the staged draft stays
  # as the rerun --failed recovery vessel (gh-1899 convention). In-flight
  # owner runs and unmarked/human drafts stay with the sweeper (E1).
  train-draft-guard:
    name: Train draft lifecycle guard
    needs: release-provenance
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    if: >-
      always() &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete the orphaned staged draft (issue #282 E2)
      actions: read # probe the draft-owner marker run's status (gh-2008 pattern)
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Delete drafts the failed train will never publish
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PROVENANCE_RESULT: ${{ needs.release-provenance.result }}
        run: bash scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

  # gh-1832 AC3: post-publish smoke. Probes (1) EVERY releases/(latest/)?
  # download/ URL the fa1.dev landing page exposes (site/index.html) and
  # (2) the full required set from scripts/release_required_assets.txt via
  # a 1-byte ranged GET each — red on anything but HTTP 200/206. Rides the
  # tag train only (PR runs never probe release URLs); a 404 here is the
  # owner-facing v1.0.635 symptom caught the same hour it appears.
  release-asset-smoke:
    name: Release asset smoke (landing links + required set)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.release-provenance.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# watchdog_trip_check.sh — the gh-2290 timeout-kill trip decision for the
# `watchdog` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml (issue #194 point 4).
#
# The watchdog's remedy for a degraded-runner allocation is ONE retrigger
# with a fresh allocation (never `gh run rerun`). Tripping requires
# recognizing a job-level timeout KILL — and only that kill. The v1.0.745
# tag run 4424840840 hung a PTY shard (the pty2 blocking-waitpid wedge,
# `Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in`), burned
# its 40-minute budget and was killed by `timeout-minutes`: GitHub landed
# that kill as job conclusion `cancelled` (NOT `failure` — jobs
# 134588877581/134566192421) with the mid-flight step `cancelled` and the
# trailing `if: always()` evidence steps `skipped`.
#
# The timeout-kill signature, as one predicate over the jobs JSON:
#
#   job conclusion == "failure" OR "cancelled"      (both kill shapes land)
#   AND at least one step concluded "cancelled"      (a step was cut
#     mid-flight — the kill itself)
#   AND NO step concluded "failure"                  (a real test failure
#     ENDS with a failed step — in these shards the `if: always()`
#     evidence steps often trail it with `success` — so a genuine red
#     never trips; a fresh runner allocation cannot fix a defect)
#
# A cancelled job with NO steps (never started — a run-level cancel
# reaching a queued job) is NOT a kill. Success/skipped never trip.
#
# Network-free by contract: the caller fetches the run's jobs document in
# ONE call (the jobs API embeds each job's steps array — `gh run view
# --json jobs`; `gh api .../runs/<id>/jobs` is fine unpaged, but
# `--paginate` concatenates page bodies and jq then reads only the first
# page — verified against a 69-job run) and hands the FILE here.
# Fixture-self-tested by scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh (#1100
# pattern), wired into the static gate; the workflow wiring is pinned by
# test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart.
#
# Usage: watchdog_trip_check.sh [jobs-json-file] [output-file]
#   jobs-json-file  the jobs document; `-` or an empty arg reads stdin
#   output-file     default $GITHUB_OUTPUT when set (the trip=<bool> line
#                   lands there AND on stdout); without one, stdout only.
#                   Diagnostics never start with `trip=`, so the line is
#                   unambiguous in both sinks.
set -u

json_file="${1:--}"
out_file="${2:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-}}"

if [ "$json_file" = "-" ] || [ -z "$json_file" ]; then
  jobs_json="$(cat)"
else
  jobs_json="$(cat "$json_file")"
fi

# The timeout-kill signature, as one jq projection:
#   failed-or-cancelled jobs with >=1 cancelled step and NO failed step.
projection='
  [.jobs[]?
   | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
   | select(any(.steps[]?; .conclusion == "cancelled"))
   | select(all(.steps[]?; .conclusion != "failure"))]
  | length'

matches="$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r "$projection")"

if [ -z "$matches" ] || ! [ "$matches" -eq "$matches" ] 2>/dev/null; then

=== publish job idempotency:
    #    daily verifyPubDev leg alarms «only release-event run(s)» loudly.
    # 2. The gate is dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict quality-gate
    #    exports — NOT the aggregate result. A red native binary/PTY leg must
    #    never hold a Dart package hostage (v1.0.520's push twin: publish
    #    skipped off a red pty-integration shard). The Provider smoke stays a
    #    hard gate (#551): needs.integration.result == 'success'.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok == 'true' &&
      needs.integration.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    concurrency:
      # push + release events both fire for PAT-pushed tags; serialize the
      # double-fire so the loser no-ops on the already-published guard below
      # instead of racing dart pub publish (version already exists → red).
      # #1368: only the push twin can publish now — the group stays as a
      # belt-and-suspenders guard for re-pushed tags.
      group: publish-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      id-token: write # OIDC — pub.dev verifies the GitHub identity, no secrets
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # A tag is a release announcement: if pubspec says publish_to: none,
      # failing LOUDLY is correct (#554) — a green skip is how pub.dev went
      # 35 versions stale unnoticed. Removing the flag from pubspec re-enables.
      - id: gate
        name: Publish gate
        run: |
          if grep -Eq '^publish_to:[[:space:]]*none' pubspec.yaml; then
            echo "::error::pubspec.yaml sets publish_to: none — a tagged release cannot reach pub.dev. Remove the flag from pubspec.yaml, or stop tagging v* releases (see #554)."
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-1452 + gh-1522: pub.dev server-rejects the upload when the
          # PACKED changelog is at/over its 262144-byte content cap
          # (v1.0.538 died mid-upload). The repo CHANGELOG.md is
          # CURATED-ONLY and is NOT what pub packs — the staged changelog
          # is trimmed under the cap by stamp_staged_release.sh before
          # upload — so an over-cap repo file must never kill the release
          # train (that is the exact #1452 class gh-1522 retired). Warn
          # loudly here; the HARD gate is the staged re-measure ahead of
          # `dart pub publish`.
          if ! bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md; then
            echo "::warning::CHANGELOG.md is at/over the pub.dev 262144-byte cap — the staged (published) changelog is trimmed to fit, so this release proceeds, but archive the tail to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (gh-1452)."
          fi
          echo "publishable=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      # gh-1522: the repo pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder — the
      # tag is the version. Guard the invariant instead of comparing the
      # tag to the placeholder: the committed pubspec must still BE the
      # placeholder (a hand-bump desyncs the tag↔staged-file invariant the
      # stamper relies on), and the staged version must equal the tag.
      - name: Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder (publish job)
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: |

.github/workflows/ci.yml
scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh
scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh
test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart
===
diff --git a/.github/workflows/ci.yml b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
index 2e1d7cc0773..6d9a73f1115 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/ci.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
@@ -804,6 +804,20 @@ jobs:
       - name: Release dedupe self-test (gh-1625)
         run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
 
+      # gh-2290: the watchdog's timeout-kill trip decision is
+      # fixture-self-tested against real jobs-API shapes — the hung
+      # v1.0.745 shard shape (conclusion `cancelled`, mid-flight step
+      # `cancelled`, trailing always()-evidence steps `skipped`), the
+      # classic failure-with-cut-step shape, real test failures in both
+      # landing shapes (failed step last AND failed step trailed by
+      # success evidence — the old last-step detector was blind to this),
+      # never-started cancels, malformed bodies failing safe, and the
+      # GITHUB_OUTPUT contract — so the release path's degraded-runner
+      # retrigger cannot rot silently before the next red tag (#1100
+      # pattern).
+      - name: Watchdog trip self-test (gh-2290)
+        run: bash scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh
+
       # #1431: the size-budget gate's own red exits are fixture-tested
       # (#1100 pattern) — an engine rev-hash rename must UPDATE not NEW,
       # vendored engine churn warns instead of reddening, first-party
@@ -4019,10 +4033,24 @@ jobs:
   # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
   # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
   # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
-  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
-  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
-  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
-  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
+  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh allocation. NEVER `gh run
+  # rerun`: it reallocates into the same degraded pool. One retrigger max
+  # per head commit / per tag (loop guards below).
+  # gh-2290: this used to be pull_request-ONLY — but since gh-1537
+  # retired the main-push CI run, v* tag pushes are the ONLY push arm
+  # this workflow receives, i.e. the release gate had NO watchdog at all.
+  # The v1.0.745 tag run 4424840840 hung a PTY shard on the pty2
+  # blocking-waitpid wedge (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate
+  # _waitForExitCode to check in`, vendor/pty2 VENDORED class), burned
+  # its 40-minute budget and was concluded `cancelled` — the aggregate
+  # gate reddened and ci-red-report filed the ticket with nothing to
+  # self-heal it. The tag arm retriggers via a `gh workflow run ci.yml
+  # --ref <tag>` dispatch (a fresh allocation; tags cannot take an
+  # empty-commit push — moving a v* tag would re-fire the release flow —
+  # and GITHUB_TOKEN MAY trigger workflow_dispatch, 2022-09-08
+  # changelog). The dispatch arm runs the full gate on the tag's exact
+  # tree: release-pending never blocks dispatch arms (gh-1551) and
+  # release-dedupe is false for non-release events (gh-1625 AC3).
   watchdog:
     name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
@@ -4031,15 +4059,37 @@ jobs:
     # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
     # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
     # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
-    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
+    # retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
     needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
-    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
-    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
-    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
+    # Same-repo PRs: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
+    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref. Tag pushes: the
+    # release gate (gh-2290).
+    if: always() && ((github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) || (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')))
     permissions:
-      actions: read
+      actions: write # gh workflow run — the tag-arm retrigger (gh-2290)
       contents: write
     steps:
+      # gh-2290: the trip decision runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's
+      # empty workspace has no scripts/ (the exit-127 class reddened the
+      # dedupe pre-check on every arm, runs 38696670029/38696668627). The
+      # checkout must be UNCONDITIONAL — the trip step runs on every arm
+      # this job reaches, and a skipped checkout would empty the trip
+      # output. Shallow: the script never reads history.
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 1
+
+      # One jobs call in a SINGLE valid document (steps arrays are
+      # embedded per job — no per-job follow-ups; `gh api --paginate`
+      # concatenates page bodies and jq then reads only the first page —
+      # verified against a 69-job run), then the extracted,
+      # fixture-self-tested trip decision (scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh;
+      # static-gate selftest: scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh). It trips
+      # ONLY on the timeout-kill signature — job conclusion `failure` OR
+      # `cancelled` (the v1.0.745 kill landed as plain `cancelled`) with
+      # at least one `cancelled` step and NO `failed` step — and never on

+# The watchdog's remedy for a degraded-runner allocation is ONE retrigger

+#   AND NO step concluded "failure"                  (a real test failure

cat <<JEOF
{"jobs": [{"name": "PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)", "conclusion": "$1", "steps": $steps}]}
JEOF
}

echo "watchdog_trip_selftest (gh-2290):"

# AC1 — the gh-2290 kill mode (the REAL shape: conclusion cancelled,
# mid-flight step cancelled, trailing always()-evidence steps skipped).
out="$(fixture ac1 "$(json_for cancelled kill)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC1 cancelled job with a cancelled step trips (gh-2290 kill mode)" $?

# AC2 — the classic kill mode (failure conclusion, cut step, no failed step).
out="$(fixture ac2 "$(json_for failure kill)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC2 failure job with a cancelled step and no failed step trips" $?

# FC1 — a real test failure must NOT retrigger (both landing shapes).
out="$(fixture fc1a '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 0/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}, {"name": "junit", "conclusion": "success"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC1a real test failure (failed step, trailing evidence) does NOT trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc1b '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 3/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "setup", "conclusion": "success"}, {"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC1b real test failure (failed LAST step) does NOT trip" $?

# FC2 — clean, skipped, never-started, empty.
out="$(fixture fc2a '{"jobs": [{"name": "Static gates", "conclusion": "success", "steps": [{"name": "analyze", "conclusion": "success"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2a success job does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2b '{"jobs": [{"name": "Golden suite (macOS baselines)", "conclusion": "skipped", "steps": []}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2b skipped job does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2c '{"jobs": [{"name": "Binaries smoke gate", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": []}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2c cancelled never-started job (no steps) does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2d '{"jobs": []}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2d empty jobs array does not trip" $?

# FC3 — malformed body fails safe.
out="$(fixture fc3 'not json at all')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC3 malformed jobs JSON fails safe to trip=false" $?
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '::warning::'
check "FC3 malformed body warns loudly" $?

# RG — output contract.
out="$(fixture rg1 "$(json_for cancelled kill)")"
[ "$(trip_count "$out")" = "1" ]
check "RG1 exactly one trip= line on stdout" $?

printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -vE '^trip=' | grep -qE '^trip='
[ $? -ne 0 ]
check "RG2 no diagnostic line masquerades as trip=" $?

out_file="$TMP/github_output"
: > "$out_file"
GITHUB_OUTPUT="$out_file" bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/ac1.json" > "$TMP/rg3.out"
grep -cE '^trip=(true|false)$' "$out_file" > "$TMP/rg3.count"
[ "$(cat "$TMP/rg3.count")" = "1" ]
check "RG3 exactly one trip= line lands in GITHUB_OUTPUT" $?

out="$(fixture rg4 '{"jobs": [{"name": "PTY shard 2/3", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "cancelled"}, {"name": "upload", "conclusion": "skipped"}]}, {"name": "PTY shard 0/3", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "cancelled"}, {"name": "upload", "conclusion": "skipped"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
[ "$(trip_count "$out")" = "1" ]
check "RG4 multiple matches trip once, one line" $?

# RG5 — stdin arm (`-`).
out="$(printf '%s' "$(json_for cancelled kill)" | bash "$CHECK" - 2>&1)"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "RG5 stdin arm trips" $?

if [ "$fails" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "watchdog_trip_selftest: $fails FAILURE(S)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "watchdog_trip_selftest: all green"

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2358 `[ci-red] v1.0.759 failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The v1.0.759 release-gate run (https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/44868070949) went red on `Build iOS (debug, unsigned)`, cascading into the aggregate `Quality gate` and `Advance vpinned marker`, with no self-heal.

**Root cause**: The `build-ios` job runs on the self-hosted `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` pool and was allocated to runner `fa-m5-1`. At 2026-11-21T05:07:54Z, ~11 minutes into the `flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)` step, the runner **lost communication with the server** (GitHub check-run annotation on job 136736814346). GitHub landed the kill as job conclusion `failure` with the mid-flight step conclusion `null` (never reported) — verified via the jobs API: 12 `success` steps, then step 13 `flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)` with `conclusion: null` and all trailing steps `null`. No product code, test, or configuration defect was involved; the 12 steps before the death (checkout, Flutter 3.50.0 setup, WasmRun restore, pub-get, sqlite3 prewarm) all succeeded on the exact tag tree, and the same run's other 47 jobs — including the same tag's Android/iOS-independent legs and `Publish to pub.dev` — were green.

**Impact**: 
1. The tag ref v1.0.759's required check runs (`Build iOS`, `Quality gate`, `Advance vpinned marker`) are red.
2. The release train died: `binaries` (Build native binaries) and `release-provenance` (Sign release checksums) are `needs`-gated on the aggregate gate and stayed SKIPPED — so no GitHub release object exists for v1.0.759 (Latest is still v1.0.758), no signed SHA256SUMS, and `fa update`/installers cannot serve it.
3. `install-pin-bump` (`Advance vpinned marker`) runs `if: always()` and failed its fail-closed pre-move provenance gate (`scripts/pin_release.sh` re-verifies the target's signed checksums before moving the marker) — by design: it refused to point `vpinned` at an unsigned release.
4. **Automation gap (the fixable part)**: the gh-2290 watchdog (`scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh`) trips ONLY on the timeout-kill signature — job `failure`/`cancelled` with ≥1 step concluded `cancelled`. A runner-death kill lands the mid-flight step as `null` (not `cancelled`), so the signature did not match, the watchdog ran, found nothing, and never dispatched a recovery run on the tag. The release train sat red until manual recovery (this leg full-reran run 44868070949).

**Recovery (already executed by this leg)**: `POST /actions/runs/44868070949/rerun` — a FULL rerun (not `--failed`: a rerun `--failed` never resurrects SKIPPED jobs, so `binaries`/`release-provenance` would stay skipped and the pin bump would fail its provenance gate again — the documented rerun-`--failed` limitation in ci.yml's `train-draft-guard` comment). The rerun re-runs the whole gate on the same tag SHA: build-ios re-allocates (the pool is healthy — `fa-m5-3` picked up jobs minutes after the incident), and a green gate unlocks `binaries` → `release-provenance` (creates + publishes the GitHub release with signed SHA256SUMS) → `install-pin-bump` (advances the vpinned marker) → release asset smoke.

**Fix approach (repo hardening, TDD)**: Extend the watchdog trip decision to also trip on the **runner-death signature**: job conclusion `failure` or `cancelled` with at least one step concluded `cancelled` OR `null` (a step cut mid-flight — either GitHub-reported cancel or a frozen unconcluded step), and NO step concluded `failure` (a real test failure ends with a failed step; a fresh runner allocation cannot fix a defect). This keeps every existing non-trip guarantee intact and gives the tag gate the same self-heal for runner death that gh-2290 gave it for timeout kills. Files: `scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh` (projection + header), `scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh` (new AC/FC fixtures), `test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart` (behavioral cases + doc), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (comment truthing for the trip decision and the static-gate self-test step).

**Previous attempt**: none — first development leg for this ticket.

# landing shapes (failed step last AND failed step trailed by
      # success evidence — the old last-step detector was blind to this),
      # never-started cancels, malformed bodies failing safe, and the
      # GITHUB_OUTPUT contract — so the release path's degraded-runner
      # retrigger cannot rot silently before the next red tag (#1100
      # pattern).
      - name: Watchdog trip self-test (gh-2290)
        run: bash scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh

      # #1431: the size-budget gate's own red exits are fixture-tested
      # (#1100 pattern) — an engine rev-hash rename must UPDATE not NEW,
      # vendored engine churn warns instead of reddening, first-party
      # payload still fails hard, and the 20+hex regex leaves first-party
      # paths that merely contain hex alone.
      - name: Size manifest gate self-test (#1431)
        run: python3 scripts/test_size_manifest.py

      # Full analyze needs the example app's package config (Flutter imports);
      # a docs-only PR skips the flutter setup entirely and analyzes the pure
      # Dart scopes only — it cannot have changed resolution anyway.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
###
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}

2. Factor the shared jq filter into a variable so the count projection and the diagnostic projection can't drift.
3. `any(.steps[]?; .conclusion == "cancelled" or .conclusion == null)`.

Careful with jq semantics: `.conclusion == null` is true when the key is missing too. A steps entry always has the key in the API, but missing-key tolerance is harmless here (a step without a conclusion is an unconcluded step).

Let me now rewrite the script precisely. Current script content I have from earlier. The relevant parts:

```bash
# The timeout-kill signature, as one jq projection:
#  job conclusion == "failure" OR "cancelled"     (both kill shapes land)
#  AND at least one step concluded "cancelled"     (a step was cut
#    mid-flight — the kill itself)
#  AND NO step concluded "failure"                 (a real test failure
#    ENDS with a failed step — in these shards the `if: always()`
#    evidence steps often trail it with `success` — so a genuine red
#    never trips; a fresh runner allocation cannot fix a defect)
#
# A cancelled job with NO steps (never started — a run-level cancel
# reaching a queued job) is NOT a kill. Success/skipped never trip.
``

and

```bash
# The timeout-kill signature, as one jq projection:
#  failed-or-canceled jobs with >=1 cancelled step and NO failed step.
projection='
 [.jobs[]?
  | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
  | select(any(.steps[]?; .conclusion == "cancelled"))
  | select(all(.steps[]?; .conclusion != "failure"))]
 | length'

matches="$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r "$projection")"
...

    | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
    | select(any(.steps[]?; .conclusion == "cancelled"))
    | select(all(.steps[]?; .conclusion != "failure"))]
   | (.[] | " " + .name + ": " + .conclusion
      + " (cancelled step: "
      + ([.steps[]? | select(.conclusion == "cancelled") | .name] | join(", "))
      + ")'
``

New version — single MATCH_FILTER variable:

```bash
# One shared jq filter for BOTH the count and the diagnostics (a
# duplicated projection can drift; the selftest pins only the trip=
# contract, the filter is the single source of truth here):
#  failed-or-canceled jobs with a mid-flight cut (>=1 step concluded
#  `cancelled` OR frozen unconcluded `null`) and NO failed step.

  | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")

and diagnostics:

```bash

      + ([.steps[]? | select(.conclusion == \"cancelled\" or .conclusion == null) | .name] | join(\", \"))
      + \")"
``

Hmm — careful with quoting: inside double-quoted bash string, embedded `"` need escaping; jq string literals with `\n`... it's fine with escapes. Actually cleaner: use a jq variable-free single-quoted heredoc? The original used two separate single-quoted jq programs. To minimize churn while keeping them in sync, I could keep two literal jq programs but update BOTH. The repo style favors explicitness. But drift risk... the dart guard test pins invocation count only. I'll go with the shared bash variable — less duplication, and the workflow passes only the file arg.

Wait — one more consideration about `.conclusion == null` in `any()`: the gh-2290 AC1 shape has trailing `skipped` steps and mid `cancelled`. The null clause now also matches... could a genuinely-green-but-concluded job have null steps? No — concluded jobs have all steps concluded (success/skipped/canceled/failure). Only runner-death freezes them. And the job-conclusion guard (`failure`/`cancelled`) plus no-failed-step guard keep it tight.

Edge: what about jobs with `conclusion: "failure"` and `steps: []` (never started but failed?) — `any()` over empty = false → no trip. Fine.

# that kill as job conclusion `cancelled` (NOT `failure` — jobs
# 134588877581/134566192421) with the mid-flight step `cancelled` and the

#
# gh-2358 added the SECOND kill shape: runner DEATH. The v1.0.759 tag run
# (44868070949, job 136736814346) lost its self-hosted runner `fa-m5-1`
# ~11 minutes into `flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)` ("The
# self-hosted runner lost communication with the server"). GitHub
# concluded the JOB `failure` but NOTHING ever reported again: the
# mid-flight step — and every trailing step — froze at conclusion `null`,
# so the `cancelled`-step-only signature was blind to it. The watchdog
# ran, found nothing, and the release train sat red (no GitHub release,
# `vpinned` marker stuck) until a manual full rerun. One trip decision,
# two kill shapes: the mid-flight cut is `cancelled` (GitHub concluded
# the cancel) or `null` (nothing ever concluded).
#
# The degraded-runner-kill signature, as one predicate over the jobs JSON:
#
#   job conclusion == "failure" OR "cancelled"      (both kill shapes land)
#   AND at least one step concluded "cancelled" OR "null"
#     (a step was cut mid-flight — the kill itself; `null` is the
#     frozen runner-death tail, gh-2358)
#   AND NO step concluded "failure"                  (a real test failure
#     ENDS with a failed step — in these shards the `if: always()`
#     evidence steps often trail it with `success` — so a genuine red
#     never trips; a fresh runner allocation cannot fix a defect. This
#     guard also covers death AFTER a real red: the failed step is
#     concluded, only the trailing steps freeze at `null`)
#
# A cancelled job with NO steps (never started — a run-level cancel
# reaching a queued job) is NOT a kill (`any()` over an empty steps
# array is false). Success/skipped never trip. A job whose conclusion
# is still null is in flight — the first select filters it out, so an
# in-progress leg can never fake the signature.

arguments.newText:
# The degraded-runner-kill signature, as ONE shared jq filter (the count
# and the diagnostics below project over the same filter — a duplicated
# literal can drift silently, and the selftest pins only the trip=
# contract): failed-or-cancelled jobs with a mid-flight cut (>=1 step
# concluded `cancelled` OR frozen unconcluded `null`) and NO failed step.
filter='.jobs[]?
   | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
   | select(any(.steps[]?; .conclusion == "cancelled" or .conclusion == null))
   | select(all(.steps[]?; .conclusion != "failure"))'

matches="$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r "[$filter] | length")"
arguments.oldText:

   | select(any(.steps[]?; .conclusion == "cancelled"))
   | select(all(.steps[]?; .conclusion != "failure"))]
  | length'

matches="$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r "$projection")"

- CI layout: `changes` (path filter) → parallel `static`, `test-core`
  (3 duration-balanced shards, `scripts/test_shards.json`, rebalanced
  weekly from junit durations; shard jobs emit junit-shard-N artifacts and
  `shard_files.py` bin-packs manifest-missing new test dirs at runtime),
  `coverage-gate`, `guards`, `flutter-tests` (ubuntu; goldens stay
  host-locked in build-macos.yml) → one aggregate `Quality gate`
  required check, plus `step-timings` (per-step duration telemetry) and a
  `watchdog` (>2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out PR leg gets ONE
  empty-commit retrigger — never `gh run rerun`, which reallocates into
  the same degraded runner pool). `perf-gate` (issue #303) folds the #262
  DoD `dart test --tags perf` trajectory gate into the aggregate for
  trajectory-touching PRs. Issue #551 adds the `integration-mock` leg to
  the aggregate for `test/integration/**` PRs (no-key legs via
  MockLlmServer); the tag-only `integration` job is just the llm provider
  smoke and `publish` waits on it. Issue #1267 N1 adds the
  `flutter-app-exzone` leg: it runs the macOS exclusion-zone family
  (`flutter_app/test/apps/` — JS-engine tests the ubuntu leg skips via
  `native_test_guard.dart`, plus `flutter_app/lib/apps/` + `lib/src/js_ext/`
  are the code that surfaces there) on macos pre-merge, closing the
  nightly-only gap the #1309 escape rode. Under this repo's dispatch-only
===
1. `ci.yml`: add `merge_group:` to the `on:` block (one line). The `changes`
   classifier already treats it as full-gate; the concurrency group
   (`ci-${{ github.ref }}`) keys off the queue branch ref — no collision with PR
   runs, and `cancel-in-progress` stays PR-only.
2. Workflows owning the other two required checks (`JS engine integration
   (quickjs-ng)`, `Binaries smoke gate`): same `merge_group:` trigger addition.
3. `watchdog` (degraded-runner retrigger) pushes an empty commit to the PR branch —
   it must stay gated to `pull_request` events; on `merge_group` there is no PR
   branch to push to. Gate it explicitly when adding the trigger.
4. `auto-update-prs.yml` (the current strict-mode coping mechanism) becomes
   unnecessary for queued repos; keep or retire as a separate decision.

# gh-2358 — [ci-red] v1.0.759 failed

### Root Cause

- The `Build iOS (debug, unsigned)` leg of tag run 44868070949 died on the self-hosted runner `fa-m5-1`: GitHub's check-run annotation reads "The self-hosted runner lost communication with the server" ~11 min into `flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)` (job 136736814346).
- GitHub landed the kill as job `failure` with the mid-flight step — and every trailing step — frozen at `conclusion: null` (nothing ever reported again). The red cascaded into the aggregate `Quality gate`, and `Advance vpinned marker` failed its fail-closed provenance pre-move gate (`scripts/pin_release.sh` refuses to point `vpinned` at an unsigned release; the release train — `binaries`/`release-provenance` — had been skipped by the red gate, so no GitHub release exists for v1.0.759).
- **Automation gap**: the gh-2290 watchdog trip decision (`scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh`) only matched the timeout-kill signature (a `cancelled` step). A runner death freezes steps at `null`, so the watchdog ran, found nothing, and never dispatched the fresh-allocation retrigger — the release train sat red until manual recovery.

### Recovery (incident closed)

- Full rerun of run 44868070949 (`POST /actions/runs/.../rerun`) — full, not `--failed`: a `--failed` rerun never resurrects SKIPPED jobs, so `binaries`/`release-provenance` would stay skipped and the pin bump would fail fail-closed again. Green gate → binaries build + attach → signed SHA256SUMS → release publish → vpinned advance → asset smoke. RESULT: see the completion comment for the final run state.

### Fix

- `scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh`: the trip decision now also matches the runner-death kill shape — job `failure`/`cancelled` with at least one step concluded `cancelled` **or frozen unconcluded (`null`)**, still guarded by "NO step concluded `failure`" so a real test red (including death after a real red) never trips. The count and the diagnostics now share one jq filter (no drift).
- `scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh`: AC3/AC3b fixtures for the runner-death shapes (encoded from the real v1.0.759 job data), FC4 for death-after-a-real-red.
- `test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart`: behavioral tests running the real script on the gh-2358 shapes; doc updated.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` + `docs/agents/quality-gates.md`: comment/doc truthing for the widened signature.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: AC3/AC3b selftest fixtures and both new dart tests failed against the old script.
- `bash scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh` — all green (AC1-AC3, FC1-FC4, RG1-RG5).
- `dart test test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart` — 19 tests passed.
- Verified against the REAL attempt-1 jobs data (job 136736814346 verbatim): the fixed decision trips on `Build iOS` alone; the `Quality gate` cascade red (a real failed step) correctly never matches.
- Full gate `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all` — result in the completion comment.

### Notes

- No product code changed — the tag tree was never defective (all 12 pre-death build steps plus every other package leg were green; `Publish to pub.dev` already succeeded on v1.0.759).
- The vpinned marker itself was healthy: it failed CLOSED rather than pointing at an unsigned release. No installer/trust-anchor action needed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pin_release.sh — advance the `vpinned` release marker to a freshly signed
# tag. PURE RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION: no commits, no pushes, no
# working-tree mutation — the marker lives entirely in GitHub Releases.
# The tag-scoped install-pin-bump CI job runs this after release-provenance
# published SHA256SUMS(.sig) for the tag.
#
# Trust model (SEC-07 #795): the marker is only a POINTER. Before it moves,
# the target release must pass check_install_pin.sh (signature verifies
# against the committed trust anchor + full platform coverage); after it
# moves, the gate runs again against the marker itself. A compromised
# marker therefore degrades to a DoS (install fails closed), never to a
# bad binary — the installer's embedded anchor is the real trust root.
#
# Usage:
#   pin_release.sh <tag>            point the vpinned marker at <tag> (vX.Y.Z)
#   pin_release.sh is-newer <a> <b> exit 0 iff semver(a) > semver(b)
#                                   (v-prefixes stripped; numeric compare)
#
# Environment:
#   GH_TOKEN             release write token (live mode)
#   PIN_RELEASE_BASE     file:// dir acting as the release root — fixture
#                        mode: the marker becomes $base/vpinned/PINNED_VERSION
#                        and no gh/network is touched (selftest/dry runs)
#   PIN_RELEASE_REPO     owner/repo for gh calls (default: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness)
#   MARKER_TAG           marker release/tag name (default: vpinned)
# POSIX-only below: Ubuntu's /bin/sh is dash — no pipefail, no arrays/[[]].
# Enable pipefail only where the shell supports it (same convention as
# site/install.sh.template).
set -eu
( set -o pipefail ) 2>/dev/null && set -o pipefail || true

MARKER="${MARKER_TAG:-vpinned}"
REPO="${PIN_RELEASE_REPO:-IstiN/flutter_agent_harness}"
BASE="${PIN_RELEASE_BASE:-https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download}"

# ── is-newer <a> <b>: numeric semver compare, v-prefix tolerated ────────────
# POSIX-pure on purpose: ubuntu runners give `sh` = dash and `awk` = mawk,
# whose printf does not apply the %010d zero-padding this compare relies on
# (the old awk ver_key made equal keys and silently reported "not newer").
